resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy (sale property)
resale_co.issued_by: Stow Creek Township Office of Housing and Zoning (Housing Officer)
requirements: Remove trash and debris inside and out; cut high grass and weeds; fix tripping hazards on walks, steps and driveways
Sheds, garages, fences and pools kept sound; pool gates self-closing and self-latching
Exterior walls, siding, roof, gutters, foundation and chimney in good repair; scrape and paint peeling paint
House numbers visible from the street, plus a 3 foot white 911 post at the end of the driveway with numbers on the left, right and street sides
Handrails on stairs with more than 4 risers; guardrails at least 30 inches high
Windows open easily and stay open, no broken glass, tight-fitting screens; exterior doors open from inside without a key
Bedroom and bathroom privacy locks; bathroom window or exhaust fan; dryer vented outside
Plumbing working and sanitary; water heater gives at least 110 degree water and has a discharge pipe about 6 inches from the floor
Heating system safe; fuel-burning appliances clear of combustibles; electrical safe and workmanlike
At least two outlets in every habitable room; grounded outlets in bathrooms and laundry; GFCI outlets within 6 feet of water and outdoors
Carbon monoxide detector outside the bedroom areas
Work done without permits must be permitted and finaled
Proof of extermination if insects or rodents are found

fees.label: Certificate of Occupancy application (sale property or rental unit)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Township's Certificate of Occupancy Application (check 'Sale Property', give owner, buyer and agent details) and mail it with the $50.00 check to Stow Creek Township, Attn: Zoning/Housing Department, PO Box 308, Shiloh, NJ 08353. Also email copies of the application and check to the Zoning Officer (Zoninghousing@stowcreektwp.org). Inspections must be completed and passed before occupancy or before personal items are placed in the home.

resale_co.notes: The Township's Land Development Ordinance (section 4.7 D) requires a certificate of occupancy on the sale or change of ownership of any property with a dwelling, and also on a change of occupants. The Certificate of Occupancy Application (October 2025) has a 'Sale Property' box and a $50.00 fee. The inspection list is the Township's 'most common Housing Inspection Violations' sheet (not a full checklist). An older 2024 version of the application listed the Housing Officer at (609)381-0828 and 900 Main Street; the current form and page give 856-455-8640 and PO Box 308. Building permits come from the Upper Deerfield Township construction office (856-455-9591) under a shared service. The Township also has a landlord rental registration.

requirements: Smoke alarms (UL listed) on every level; battery-only alarms must be the 10-year sealed battery type, and hardwired alarms cannot be replaced with battery alarms
Basement smoke alarm at the bottom of the stairwell, on the ceiling (not between joists)
A 10-year sealed smoke alarm in every bedroom
Smoke alarms and CO alarms must be less than 10 years old and working
Carbon monoxide alarm in the hallway within 10 feet of all bedrooms
House numbers at least 4 inches high, contrasting color, permanently fixed and visible from the street
Homes with solar panels, a backup generator or battery storage need a permanent printed 'Caution: Multiple Sources of Power' label at the main electrical panel and the electric meter

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the online 'CO and Smoke Certification Application' (Google Form) linked from the Bridgeton Fire Department's Uniform Fire Code page and pick Stow Creek Township as the municipality. Payment is by check or money order payable to the City of Bridgeton Fire Department (the form says an online payment link will be on the invoice). The certificate is valid for 90 days. Questions: firedepartment@cityofbridgeton.com or 856-451-0090 (guideline sheet) / (856) 451-0091 (Bureau of Fire Prevention).
authorities.contact_title: Fire Official and Chief of Department, City of Bridgeton Fire Department

evidence.quote: The City of Bridgeton Fire Department is the local enforcing agency who is responsible for the enforcement of the Uniform Fire Safety Act within the City of Bridgeton, Hopewell Township, Greenwich Township, Stow Creek Township, Shiloh Borough, Fairfield Township, Downe Township, and Alloway Township.

Jack Justice Jr. serves as the appointed fire official overseeing a staff of 3 full time fire inspectors, as well as 4 part time fire inspectors. Inspectors work varying schedules, so if you need to contact them utilize their email or contact the Bureau of Fire Prevention at (856) 451-0091.

fire_cert.notes: The DCA registry lists Stow Creek Township as F, and its shared-service note says Bridgeton City is the LEA for 'Stowe Creek Township'; the City of Bridgeton Fire Department's Uniform Fire Code page names Stow Creek Township, and its online smoke/CO application lists Stow Creek Township as a municipality choice. The Township's own housing violations sheet says a passing fire inspection report from the Bridgeton Fire Department is required. Fees, lead time and the 90-day validity come from the Bridgeton Bureau's guideline sheet (created November 20, 2025); the middle tier is printed as '7 business days prior'. No fire extinguisher is listed (P.L.2025, c.19). Firefighting is by the Hopewell-Stow Creek Fire Department (non-emergency 856-453-1400), which does not issue certificates.

other_items.label: Fire inspection report from the Bridgeton Fire Department
other_items.detail: The Township's housing inspection list says a passing fire inspection report is required from the Bridgeton Fire Department.

other_items.label: Septic certification or waiver
other_items.detail: If there is a septic system, a passing certification or waiver from the County Health Department is required.

other_items.label: Water certificate
other_items.detail: A passing water certificate from the County Health Department is required.

other_items.label: Chimney inspection for wood stoves
other_items.detail: If there is a wood burning stove, a passing inspection report from a licensed chimney contractor or inspector is required.

other_items.label: Open or missing construction permits
other_items.detail: Work done without building permits must be permitted and final inspections completed (Upper Deerfield construction office).
